| [QUESTION-103](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-103.md) | Is computational indistinguishability the bounded-observer form of signal detection's chance ROC, and is ideal-observer efficiency its empirical measure, so that the record's formal results on bounded observers can be tested on real ones? | The owner asked whether material downstream of computational indistinguishability, or the signal detection literature, would help. A test's distinguishing advantage is its hit rate minus its false-alarm rate, a point on its ROC; the best over all tests is total variation, reached by the likelihood-ratio detector ([THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md)). Computational indistinguishability says every efficient observer's ROC stays near the chance diagonal. Ideal-observer analysis measures how far real observers fall short of the ideal. This asks whether the two are one framework. | Open |

| [QUESTION-114](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-114.md) | Is sorting a collection amortized search, and does physical database design, where a table is stored in one order and every further index is paid for in space and upkeep, give the joint cost model that the question on amortized retrieval lacks? | The LEGO parable ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) is [QUESTION-095](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-095.md)'s trade in its plainest form. | [QUESTION-121](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-121.md) | Within a single mind, what plays the part of the operator model's independent scoring: what evidence reaches a judgement–observation loop, or what scores it, without passing through the interpretation it tests, and does any of it survive the loss of all action? | Left open by [CLAIM-342](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-342.md), which says what anchors a judgement–observation loop is evidence whose arrival or scoring does not pass through the interpretation it tests, as Regime B's independent scoring does in [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md).
